verses.english: Linked Discourses 47.7
1. In Ambapālī’s Mango Grove
A Monkey

verses.pali: “Atthi, bhikkhave, himavato pabbatarājassa duggā visamā desā, yattha neva makkaṭānaṁ cārī na manussānaṁ.
verses.english: “Mendicants, in the Himalayas there are regions that are rugged and impassable. In some such regions, neither monkeys nor humans can go,

verses.pali: Atthi, bhikkhave, himavato pabbatarājassa duggā visamā desā, yattha makkaṭānañhi kho cārī, na manussānaṁ.
verses.english: while in others, monkeys can go but not humans.

verses.pali: Atthi, bhikkhave, himavato pabbatarājassa samā bhūmibhāgā ramaṇīyā, yattha makkaṭānañceva cārī manussānañca.
verses.english: There are also level, pleasant places where both monkeys and humans can go.

verses.pali: Tatra, bhikkhave, luddā makkaṭavīthīsu lepaṁ oḍḍenti makkaṭānaṁ bādhanāya.
verses.english: There hunters set snares of tar on the monkey trails to catch the monkeys.

verses.pali: Tatra, bhikkhave, ye te makkaṭā abālajātikā alolajātikā, te taṁ lepaṁ disvā ārakā parivajjanti.
verses.english: The monkeys who are not foolhardy and reckless see the tar and avoid it from afar.

verses.pali: Yo pana so hoti makkaṭo bālajātiko lolajātiko, so taṁ lepaṁ upasaṅkamitvā hatthena gaṇhāti.
verses.english: But a foolish and reckless monkey goes up to the tar and grabs it with a hand.
He gets stuck there.
Thinking to free his hand, he grabs it with his other hand.
He gets stuck there.
Thinking to free both hands, he grabs it with a foot.
He gets stuck there.

verses.pali: ‘Ubho hatthe mocessāmi pādañcā’ti dutiyena pādena gaṇhāti.
verses.english: Thinking to free both hands and foot, he grabs it with his other foot.
He gets stuck there.

verses.pali: ‘Ubho hatthe mocessāmi pāde cā’ti tuṇḍena gaṇhāti.
verses.english: Thinking to free both hands and feet, he grabs it with his snout.
He gets stuck there.

verses.pali: Evañhi so, bhikkhave, makkaṭo pañcoḍḍito thunaṁ seti anayaṁ āpanno byasanaṁ āpanno yathākāmakaraṇīyo luddassa.
verses.english: And so the monkey, trapped at five points, just lies there screeching. He’d meet with tragedy and disaster, and the hunter can do what he wants with him.

verses.pali: Tamenaṁ, bhikkhave, luddo vijjhitvā tasmiṁyeva kaṭṭhakataṅgāre avassajjetvā yena kāmaṁ pakkamati.
verses.english: The hunter spears him on that very banana tree, pries him off, and goes wherever he wants.

verses.pali: Evaṁ so taṁ, bhikkhave, hoti yo agocare carati paravisaye.
verses.english: That’s what happens when you roam out of your territory into the domain of others.

verses.pali: Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, mā agocare carittha paravisaye.
verses.english: So, mendicants, don’t roam out of your own territory into the domain of others.

verses.pali: Agocare, bhikkhave, carataṁ paravisaye lacchati māro otāraṁ, lacchati māro ārammaṇaṁ.
verses.english: If you roam out of your own territory into the domain of others, Māra will find a vulnerability and get an opportunity.

verses.pali: Ko ca, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno agocaro paravisayo?
verses.english: And what is not a mendicant’s own territory but the domain of others?
It’s the five kinds of sensual stimulation.
What five?

verses.pali: Cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā,
verses.english: Sights known by the eye, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.
Sounds known by the ear …
Smells known by the nose …
Tastes known by the tongue …

verses.pali: kāyaviññeyyā phoṭṭhabbā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
verses.english: Touches known by the body, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.
This is not a mendicant’s own territory but the domain of others.

verses.pali: Gocare, bhikkhave, caratha sake pettike visaye.
verses.english: You should roam inside your own territory, the domain of your fathers.

verses.pali: Gocare, bhikkhave, carataṁ sake pettike visaye na lacchati māro otāraṁ, na lacchati māro ārammaṇaṁ.
verses.english: If you roam inside your own territory, the domain of your fathers, Māra won’t find a vulnerability and get an opportunity.

verses.pali: Ko ca, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno gocaro sako pettiko visayo?
verses.english: And what is a mendicant’s own territory, the domain of the fathers?
It’s the four kinds of mindfulness meditation.
What four?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ;
verses.english: It’s when a mendicant meditates by observing an aspect of the body—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.
They meditate observing an aspect of feelings …
mind …

verses.pali: dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ.
verses.english: principles—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno gocaro sako pettiko visayo”ti.
verses.english: This is a mendicant’s own territory, the domain of the fathers.”
